key_insight: Parallel-Synthesis lets an LLM synthesizer directly read parallel branch KV caches instead of concatenating branch text, preserving branch structure while cutting redundant computation.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more native and efficient interface for multi-agent workflows, especially when many independent branches must be merged quickly.
method: Cache mapper calibrates KV caches from independently generated worker branches.
Fine-tuned synthesizer adapter generates from a non-sequential cache interface.
Training uses parallel-cache contexts plus distillation from standard text-concatenation synthesis.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on nine datasets across math, science QA, code, GAIA, and database diagnosis; it matches or exceeds text-based synthesis on seven and reduces time-to-first-token by 2.5x-11x.
watch_item: Direct cache-based synthesis depends on careful cache alignment/calibration, so robustness across heterogeneous branch lengths, models, or retrieval styles may be implementation-sensitive.
paper_title: Towards Direct Latent-Space Synthesis for Parallel Branches in LLM-Agent Workflows
